Weight is recorded per bunny. Choose a bunny from the switcher to see its history.
No weighings recorded yet. Three are needed before a trend can be judged at all.
%1$s on %2$s is removed from the history, and the trend is worked out again without it.
Nothing to plot yet. A chart needs at least two weighings.
One weighing so far. A second gives the chart a line to draw.
Only one weighing in %1$s, so there is no line to draw. There are earlier ones.
No weighings in %1$s. The most recent one was on %2$s.
Whole grams, as the scale reads it.
When the bunny was on the scale
Defaults to now. Weigh in the morning and log it in the evening if that suits — the time you set is the one that counts.

resources.string: Those two weighings are %1$s apart, so this is a change over a long stretch rather than a sudden one.
This is an observation about the numbers, not a diagnosis. If you are worried, ask a vet.
On a vet-directed diet? Then this is the loss you are aiming for, and you can ignore these.
This changes how weights are shown, not how they are entered — entry is always in grams, and changes are always shown in grams.
Export your records to a file, restore them from one, and see the copies kept on this phone.
Binky can use a different language from the rest of the phone. Changing this restarts the app.

Binky keeps your bunnies\' health history on this phone — weights, observations and photos. There is no account and no server: nothing you record here is sent anywhere.\n\nThree quick questions, and then it is yours.
%1$s is in. You can add more bunnies at any time from the switcher at the top of the screen.
Your bunnies are in. You can add more at any time from the switcher at the top of the screen.
Everything lives on this phone, which means a lost phone is a lost history unless something is copying it. Two different things can, and neither one covers everything.
Binky cannot tell whether it is switched on, and cannot switch it on for you. Now is a good moment to check.
This is what an export you make yourself will contain. It is also the default you can change later.
All of this stays editable in Settings › Backup & restore.
Binky can remind you about recurring care — a nail trim every six weeks, a yearly vaccination, a weekly weigh-in. Reminders arrive once a day, on this phone only, and you choose what they are for.
Notifications are off, so reminders will only appear inside the app.
Reminders are on. This phone may still delay or drop them while Binky is in the background — the setting below is what fixes that.
Reminders are on, and this phone is set up to let them through.
No problem. You can turn them on whenever you like.
Android will not ask again, so this one has to be switched on in the phone\'s settings.
One more thing, or reminders may not arrive

Android pauses apps it thinks are idle, and a paused Binky cannot post a reminder. Exempting it from battery optimisation is what lets a reminder through at nine in the morning after the phone has been asleep all night.
Some phones — Xiaomi above all — also keep an autostart list of their own. Binky cannot read it, so it cannot tell you whether it is set; this is just the way in.
Debug builds only. Adds two bonded bunnies, a year of uneven, back-dated weighings and a handful of observations, so the chart, the trend flag and the timeline can be reviewed against real history.
The sample bunnies are already here.

Debug builds only. Posts one notification two minutes from now, on its own path rather than through the daily sweep — so the channel, the permission and the delivery can be proven with no reminders in existence.
A test reminder will arrive in two minutes. Lock the phone and wait.
This is what a care reminder will look like. Nothing is due — the reminder was scheduled by hand from Settings.
Nail trims, vaccinations, weigh-ins, and anything else you have set a recurring reminder for.
A once-a-day nudge to look in on a bunny you are watching closely. Only while a watch is running.
An occasional prompt to export your records, at the interval you chose. Nothing to do with any bunny.
Android backs Binky up to your Google account on its own schedule — when the phone is idle, charging and online. Binky cannot switch that on or check it for you.
No automatic backup has been recorded on this phone.
The last automatic backup was on %1$s — more than two weeks ago. Something may have turned it off.
It covers your records, your settings and your bunny avatars. Your photo gallery is not in it.
Your records, your settings, and bunny avatars. The smallest useful backup.
Everything in Essential, plus scanned documents — everything you might need again.
Everything in Records, plus your photo gallery. Much larger, and the only backup your photos ever get.

Your photos are the least protected thing in Binky. Android\'s automatic backup leaves the gallery out, and so do Essential and Records. An “Everything” export is the only copy your photos will ever have.
An export normally goes to the share sheet and you choose what to do with it. You can also pick a folder — on this phone, or in a cloud app like Drive — and Binky will write straight there.
No folder chosen. Exports go to the share sheet.
Binky can no longer write to the folder you chose. It may have been moved or deleted, or its permission withdrawn. Choose it again, or carry on using the share sheet.
Binky could not write to that folder, so the backup was shared instead — nothing was lost. If it keeps happening, choose a folder on this phone.
This phone would not let Binky keep access to that folder, so no folder was saved. Exports still go to the share sheet.
This phone has no file picker Binky can open, so exports go to the share sheet.
A nudge to make an export, arriving at the same time of day as your other reminders. It is a prompt about your backups, not a sign that anything is wrong.
Notifications are off for Binky, or muted for backup reminders, so this one cannot arrive.
Time to back up your records?
You asked to be reminded. Open Backup & restore to make a fresh export — it takes a couple of taps.
Restoring replaces everything Binky currently holds with what is inside the file. A copy of the current records is saved to this phone first, so a restore can be undone.
%1$s backup from %2$s.\n\nEverything Binky currently holds is replaced. A copy of the current records is saved to this phone first.
This file is not a Binky backup. Nothing on this phone was changed.
This backup was made by a newer version of Binky, which this one cannot read. It was saved at version %1$d, and this app reads up to version %2$d. Nothing on this phone was changed.
This file is far too large to be a Binky backup. Nothing on this phone was changed.
Binky could not open the records inside this backup, so nothing was changed. The file may be damaged.

No copies have been saved on this phone.
%1$s is removed from this phone for good. If you have not shared it somewhere else, it is gone.
Saved before an update cleared the records

Defaults to now. Checked the tray this morning and are writing it up tonight? Set the time you looked — that is the one that counts.

%1$s is archived, so this cannot cover them.
%1$s is under a watch — log for them separately.
Recorded once, for everyone this covers — a shared tray cannot be told apart per bunny.
I looked, and saw none of these
Worth ticking. An empty list on its own only means nobody checked.
No observations recorded yet. Anything you notice — the tray, the mood, a symptom — belongs here.
The observation recorded on %1$s is removed.
This observation covered %1$s. Deleting it removes it for all of them.
Records the ordinary day: droppings normal, eating and drinking as usual, bright and active.
Nothing scheduled yet. A care reminder is a job that comes round again — a nail trim, a yearly vaccination, a weekly weigh-in.
Care is per bunny. Which one?
Today unless you say otherwise. The next one is scheduled from the day it was actually done, so a late trim resets the interval rather than owing it.
That day has not happened yet.
Weighing is what completes this one, so it opens the weight form. Any weighing counts, whenever you record it.
Nothing recorded yet. Recording a completion is what moves the next date.
Weighings count as weigh-ins. They are edited and deleted on the Weight screen, not here.
Removing the completion recorded on %1$s moves every occurrence after it.
Hands this repeat to your calendar app once, where it survives a new phone. Binky does not keep the two in step afterwards — editing the reminder here changes nothing there.
There is no calendar app on this phone to hand it to.
Your own words, so this one stays as you typed it whichever language Binky is in.
Give it a name so you know what it is.
Not when you last did it — when it is next owed, which is what a vet card tells you. If you do know when it was last done, record that below as a completion.
%1$s goes, and every completion recorded against it. Weighings are not touched.
Each morning Binky asks whether you have checked on them. Logging anything for that bunny settles the day — a healthy day counts. It stops on its own when the time is up.
The watch on %1$s has run out
It has already stopped asking. Extend it if you are still keeping an eye out, or close it.
Nothing has been weighed, so there is no trend to show either way.
A watch is running. Whatever you saw is worth writing down — a healthy day counts.
